reason: The finding is confirmed on both governance and code. (1) Code: tools/trainlab.py l.755 defines the original clause 'new_fork_precision_ge_0.35' as new_tp / ALL new forks. l.781 'kept' removes it, l.795-796 pass_strict_plateau_L2 = kept AND L2, and decisions() sets in_force = pass_strict_plateau_L2. The line numbers in the finding are off by about 14. (2) Math: evaluable precision TP/(TP+FP) is always >= TP/all. Wilson z=1.2816 on 3/6 gives 0.2682 > 0.265, so the finding's example fails the original clause (0.30) but passes L2. L2 as a whole is therefore NOT strictly tighter than the original gate. (3) Rule: FINAL_REPORT_v4.md l.9 says everything that loosens a gate is marked [needs OK]. ADDENDUM L (CONTEXT 18:20 UTC) labels L2 '[bug fix + tightening]' with no [OK], so the loosening half was never put to the user. Mitigations, which make this weaker but not refuted: L2 was pre-registered before the exp60 dumps (downloaded 20:05), so it is not a data-driven change. The round-1 D3 verifiers deliberately designed the Wilson bound to 'replace the bare 0.35 point estimate'. The original clause is a measurement bug: free forks on unannotated cells sit in its denominator. Practical effect, which the finding understates: only ~3.3% of forks are evaluable (exp39 66/2014), so TP/all is ~<=0.03 for t*<0.25. 'Original AND L2' in force therefore means K3b cannot pass until the user OKs L2. That costs about zero, because S5 (K3b) is 26 Sep 11:00-14:00 UTC and the user's morning OK (~05:00) comes first. The exp60 T9 results.md is not on disk yet, so the rule can still be fixed before anyone reads the DeepCenter verdict. Value lens: 0 score gain. The original clause does not predict private better; the whole merit is rule discipline, which is this team's remit.
fix: Before reading the exp60 T9 DeepCenter verdict: (a) Add a CONTEXT.md line: 'K3b in force until the user's OK on L2 = original T9 strict (including new_fork_precision_ge_0.35 over ALL new forks) AND L2; L2 re-classified as [OK] because the evaluable denominator loosens the precision clause.' (b) Make a small additive change to trainlab.decisions()/decisions_text(): a key 'strict_orig_precision_plus_L2' = dc['pass_strict'] AND all(L2 checks), set as in_force, printed as a third line in results.md next to new_precision (all) and new_precision_evaluable, new_tp/new_fp/ignored counts. Existing keys stay unchanged. Run the 112-test suite. (c) In the morning brief, ask the user explicitly to OK L2, with its reason (original clause about 0.03 by construction, since about 97% of new forks are metric-free) and a warning that without the OK K3b is off. No kernel, runtime or LB effect.
realistic_gain: 0 score, private or public. Governance only: it keeps the 'loosen -> [OK]' rule intact at ~15 min CPU/code cost with no schedule loss, because the user's OK comes before S5. Without the OK, K3b is effectively closed, which is the expected outcome anyway (P(L2 pass) ~0.1-0.15 per round-1 D3).
